## Recipes

### Anticipation & near-miss
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/
Tags: anticipation, tension, scatter, near-miss, spine, horizontal, reverse, curve, acceleration

Every way to hold the player at the reel stop, from a single slowed reel to a full Spine near-win act.

#### Anticipate a reel

Slow the closing reels (3 and 4) to build tension before they land.

Live demo (anticipate-a-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/

#### Anticipation teaser

Pair setAnticipation with a `bufferStart` prefill so a chosen symbol sits at the top edge, approaching but never landing, while the slow reels decelerate.

Live demo (anticipation-teaser): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/

#### Teaser on a reel that spins up

The same teaser on a `direction('reverse')` set. Buffers are geometric, so `bufferStart` is still the slot above the window - which on a reverse reel is the side symbols have already left.

**Gotcha:** park the teaser on the feed edge, not on `bufferStart` out of habit. `reel.axis.feedEdge` reports `'start'` on a forward reel and `'end'` on a reverse one, so one branch covers both.

Live demo (anticipation-reverse-teaser): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#anticipation-reverse-teaser

#### Scatter-driven anticipation

Pick the tease reels straight from the result grid with anticipationForScatters.

Live demo (scatter-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#scatter-anticipation

#### Tension on a horizontal set

Scatter-driven anticipation with the strips running sideways. `anticipationForScatters` scans reels 0, 1, 2, 3 and `setAnticipation` holds the trailing ones, exactly as on a vertical set - reel index is orientation-neutral, so no tension code branches.

**Gotcha:** what changes is where those reels sit. On a horizontal set reels march down the screen, so "the last two reels tease" plays as the bottom two rows crawling sideways, not as the rightmost columns.

Live demo (anticipation-horizontal-scatter): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#anticipation-horizontal-scatter

#### Staggered / sequential anticipation

Tease reels one after another instead of all slowing at once.

Live demo (staggered-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#staggered-anticipation

#### Slowing anticipation

Each teasing reel crawls slower than the last, then stops exactly there.

Live demo (slowing-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#staggered-anticipation

#### Anticipation in turbo

Keep the tease playing in Turbo / SuperTurbo with a duration override (the SuperTurbo profile sets anticipationDelay to 0, so a plain call skips the tease).

Live demo (turbo-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#turbo-anticipation

#### Shape the tease: surge, then crawl

The stock tease only decelerates, and an ease applied to a SPEED is a step in acceleration - `power2.out` puts peak deceleration on the first frame, so the reel reads as being *set* to a lower speed rather than slowing down.

`curve` replaces the fixed shape with explicit legs. Speeds are multiples of `spinSpeed`, so `2` is a genuine surge and `0.08` a crawl; segment eases default to `power2.inOut`, which ramps the acceleration in *and* out.

```ts
reelSet.setAnticipation([2, 3, 4], {
  stagger: 260,
  curve: [
    { speed: 2,    duration: 240, ease: 'power2.in' },
    { speed: 0.08, duration: 620, ease: 'power3.inOut', hold: 300 },
  ],
});
```

**Gotcha:** `curve` and `slowdown` together throws - `slowdown` is shorthand for a two-leg curve. The profile's `anticipationDelay` still gates whether the tease runs at all, so Turbo needs a `duration` override; the curve's own durations set the length.

Live demo (anticipation-surge-curve): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#anticipation-surge-curve

#### A different curve per reel

Two curves of different lengths have no meaningful midpoint, so `curve` takes a function - `(order, total) => AnticipationSegment[]` - instead of interpolating.

**Gotcha:** `order` is the reel's place in the anticipation set, not its index. `setAnticipation([4, 2, 3], ...)` hands `order: 0` to reel 4, matching `slowdown` and `protect: 'stepwise'`.

Live demo (anticipation-curve-per-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#anticipation-curve-per-reel

#### Tease for N symbols, not N milliseconds

`duration` is a time budget, so how far a reel moves depends on its speed. When the tease is choreographed around symbols passing the window - "three more and it lands" - anchor to travel instead: `cells: n` ends it after n symbol pitches, read off a monotonic odometer (`reel.travelledCells`) that survives the snap at the end of every spin. `cells` takes the same function-of-order form as `curve`.

**Gotcha:** the anchor applies to the FINAL leg; earlier legs always play in full, or a fast opening segment would silently delete the ones after it. `duration` is the backstop on that leg, since a reel at rest can never reach a travel target.

Live demo (anticipation-cells): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#anticipation-cells

#### The gas pedal: bounded acceleration

An ease shapes only the transition it was written for. `motionModel('drive', ...)` bounds acceleration instead: phases assign `reel.targetSpeed` and `Reel.update` walks the speed toward it, so every transition inherits the same feel, interruption is a single reassignment, and `jerkFrames` ramps the acceleration itself.

```ts
builder.motionModel('drive', { accelFrames: 20, decelFrames: 34, jerkFrames: 260 })
```

Bounds are profile-relative - frames to the ACTIVE profile's full speed - because the presets run `spinSpeed` 30 / 50 / 80 and one absolute px/frame^2 bound would make SuperTurbo start slower than Normal. The absolute `{ accel, decel, jerk }` form still works for a single-profile game; mixing the two throws.

**Gotcha:** build-time only, and opt-in - the default `'tween'` model is byte-for-byte unchanged. Landing and a skip press stay instantaneous by design, exactly as they are under `'tween'`. A segment the drive cannot reach in time says so on the notice channel.

Live demo (anticipation-drive): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#anticipation-drive

#### Driving tease audio

`anticipation:reel` and `anticipation:reelEnd` bracket a tension loop. `anticipation:segment` (`{ reelIndex, index, total, speed, targetSpeed }`) fires once per curve leg, so a surge can sound different from the crawl after it without polling for the boundary. For a pitch ramp that tracks the actual slow-down, sample `reelSet.reels[i].speedNormalized` from your own ticker: `1` at full blur, `0` at rest, above `1` during a surge.

#### Skip the tease

Let the player slam through a long anticipation at any point.

Live demo (skip-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#skip-anticipation

#### Skip that cannot hide the tease

The same long tease, but the first press only lands the reels AROUND it. `protect: 'once'` guarantees the two scatters are on screen and the build-up is visibly under way before a second press can end it.

**Gotcha:** call `setAnticipation` BEFORE `setResult`. A press in the pre-result window is queued by `requestSkip()` and fires the instant the result arrives, so the tease has to be registered by then or there is nothing to protect.

Live demo (protected-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#protected-anticipation

`protect: 'stepwise'` walks it forward one reel per press instead of ending it in one go. That, partial slams, per-reel spin floors, and why a protected tease beats a slower skip are all on [Skip & slam](/recipes/skip/).

#### Scatter jaw anticipation

The rig's own near-win clips - the leftmost scatter snaps its jaw, holds the loop, and the rightmost lands the verdict.

Live demo (spine-scatter-jaw-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#spine-scatter-jaw-anticipation

#### Fake a near-miss

Place N-1 scatters plus anticipation on the reel that "almost" landed one.

**Gotcha:** the grid always resolves to a loss; deliberately engineered near-misses are restricted in some jurisdictions, so confirm with compliance before shipping.

Live demo (near-miss): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/anticipation/#near-miss

### Big symbols & non-uniform grids
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/
Tags: big-symbols, multiways, pyramid, spine, geometry, sticky-wild, horizontal, reverse, orientation

Everything for N-by-M block symbols and non-uniform reel geometry, one live demo at a time.

#### MxN big symbols. every shape

Square 2x2, tall 1x3, giant 3x3, wide 2x4, one focused demo per shape.

Live demo (big-symbols-mxn-square): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbols-mxn
Live demo (big-symbols-mxn-tall): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbols-mxn
Live demo (big-symbols-mxn-giant): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbols-mxn
Live demo (big-symbols-mxn-wide): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbols-mxn

#### Tall blocks that stream past during the spin

A 1x3 block with a weight scrolls on reel 0 while it spins, and a scatter only ever scrolls on reel 4. Both weights live in per-reel pools: `0` in the base `weights()` table, raised on the one reel that may show the symbol. Only blocks one reel wide can carry a weight; wider ones still land only, since the random fill feeds one reel at a time.

**Gotcha:** a pool `exclude` cannot be lifted again by a narrower layer, a weight of `0` can. Use weights, not `exclude`, for "this symbol on this reel only". And a weighted block needs `bufferSymbols({ start: size.cells })`, which the builder checks: the block enters a forward reel bottom first and leaves a reverse reel anchor first, and those buffer slots are where its covered cells sit while the anchor that draws them is off the strip.

Live demo (tall-symbols-in-spin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#tall-symbols-in-spin

#### Tall block in an anticipation tease, landing peeking, then up

Two scatters put reel 4 into a crawl, and the weighted 1x3 keeps sliding past while it crawls. The result lands the block with its head on the last visible cell and its body in `bufferEnd` (so `bufferSymbols({ start: 3, end: 2 })`: `start` for the weight, `end` for the peek). Then the game brings it up, two ways:

- **Nudge up.** `nudge(reel, { distance: 2, direction: 'reverse' })` moves the whole column; the two cards above scroll out through the top.
- **Expand up.** The landed anchor is already one sprite three cells tall with its body under the mask. Tween its view up two cells and it grows over the cards, then `setColumn(reel, { visible: ['tall', ...] })` commits the block at the top of the column while the rest of the board stays put. An expanding wild, in engine terms.

**Gotcha:** `getBlockBounds` reports the whole block even while part of it hangs in a buffer; the mask does the clipping.

Live demo (tall-peek-nudge-up): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#tall-peek
Live demo (tall-peek-expand-up): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#tall-peek

#### Big symbol falls into view through a cascade

A tall wild lands with its anchor in bufferStart and only its tail showing, wins the cells below, and falls into full view as they clear; the 2x2 canvas runs the same beat across two reels.

**Gotcha:** the anchor's fall distance must equal the number of winner cells cleared below it, or the block snaps instead of falling.

Live demo (big-symbol-cascade-fall): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbol-cascade-fall
Live demo (big-symbol-cascade-fall-2x2): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbol-cascade-fall

#### Land a big symbol partially in buffer

A tall 1xH block lands with its anchor in bufferStart, so only the bottom tail shows at cell 0; nudge down to drag the rest into view.

Live demo (big-symbol-partial-land): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbol-partial-land

#### Nudge a big symbol in, then hold it across a respin

Nudge the tail-visible wild fully into view, then respin the other reels with `holdReels` so the revealed block stays put.

Live demo (big-symbol-held-respin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbol-held-respin

#### Big symbol on a horizontal set

A 2x3 block on `.orientation('horizontal')`, outlined on land with `getBlockBounds`. `size: { reels, cells }` is index space and does not rotate: `reels` always spans the reel-marching axis, `cells` always spans the strip.

**Gotcha:** the screen mapping inverts. `{ reels: 2, cells: 3 }` is 2 wide and 3 tall on a vertical set, 2 tall and 3 wide here, and `getBlockBounds` (screen space) inverts with it.

Live demo (big-symbols-horizontal-block): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbols-horizontal-block

#### Tail-visible block on a roll-up reel

The partial-land tease on a `.direction('reverse')` reel: the block is anchored at the last visible cell with its body hanging into `bufferEnd`, then a `'forward'` nudge (upward, on this reel) drags it into full view.

**Gotcha:** buffers are geometric, not travel-relative. `bufferStart` is above and `bufferEnd` below in both directions, so a reel that feeds from the bottom teases out of `bufferEnd`.

Live demo (big-symbols-reverse-tail): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#big-symbols-reverse-tail

#### getBlockBounds. outline a big symbol

One rectangle that hugs an entire block whichever cell you pass; a 1x1 returns the same rect as `getCellBounds`.

Live demo (get-block-bounds): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#get-block-bounds

#### Big symbols with Spine

Same 2x2 anchor mechanic, every cell a Spine skeleton; the bigWild reuses the wild rig scaled to the larger block.

Live demo (spine-big-symbols): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#spine-big-symbols

#### MultiWays

Per-spin cell variation: each reel lands on a different cell count and the total ways is the product of the per-reel cells.

**Gotcha:** call `setShape(cellsPerReel)` BEFORE `setResult()` on every spin.

Live demo (multiways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#spine-big-symbols

#### MultiWays cascade

Per-spin shape on a strip-spin landing, then cascade tumbling that pops ways winners and drops new symbols in from above.

**Gotcha:** `setShape` before `setResult`, and open with `spin({ mode: 'standard' })` so AdjustPhase reshapes between SPIN and STOP.

Live demo (multiways-cascade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#spine-big-symbols

#### Per-reel shape (pyramid)

A non-uniform reel set (3-5-5-5-3), static shape declared at build via `visibleCellsPerReel`.

Live demo (pyramid-shape): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#pyramid-shape

#### Pyramid shape with Spine

The same 3-5-5-5-3 pyramid with every cell a Spine skeleton, crisp at every per-reel cell size.

Live demo (spine-pyramid-shape): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#spine-pyramid-shape

#### Sticky wild on MultiWays

A pin survives every reshape via its remembered `originCell` (the default `migration: 'origin'`): it clamps when the shape shrinks and restores when it grows back. `'frozen'` is the opposite -- each clamp rewrites the origin, so it never climbs back.

Live demo (sticky-wild-multiways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/big-symbols/#sticky-wild-multiways

### Cascade & tumble
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/
Tags: cascade, tumble, refill, anticipation, spine, thunderkick, horizontal, reverse, orientation, gravity

The full cascade and tumble toolkit, one live demo at a time.

#### Cascade 6x4 tumble

Modern tumble mechanic where `runCascade` owns the detect, destroy, refill loop; the second canvas is the identical recipe on real Thunderkick Spine art.

Live demo (cascade-6x5): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#cascade-6x5
Live demo (cascade-6x5-spine): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#cascade-6x5

#### Cascade wins. present, destroy, refill

The fixed round order (present the win, destroy the winners, refill the holes), then the destroy stage two ways: the engine implode versus an authored Spine explosion.

**Gotcha:** compute winners from your match logic, never by diffing two grids. survivors slide past cleared slots and a diff misreads them.

Live demo (destroy-winpresenter): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#cascade-destroy-and-present
Live demo (destroy-fade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#cascade-destroy-and-present
Live demo (destroy-explode): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#cascade-destroy-and-present

#### Lead-in delay before the fall

#### Spin first, cascade after

Open every play with a classic strip-spin, then cascade the respins; the per-spin `mode` override flips between strip-spin and pure drop.

Live demo (spin-then-cascade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#spin-then-cascade
Live demo (cascade-open-drop): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#spin-then-cascade
Live demo (spin-then-cascade-turbo): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#spin-then-cascade

#### Cascade sideways

The same tumble on `.orientation('horizontal')`: reels are screen rows, the strip travels along X, and `tumble({ gravity })` stays on its default `'auto'`, so each reel drains toward the edge it travels toward and refills from the other one.

**Gotcha:** gravity decides the server contract. survivors must be packed against the edge gravity exits by (`[...fresh, ...survivors]` under forward gravity). The engine animates the grid you send, it never reorders it.

Live demo (cascade-horizontal-tumble): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#cascade-horizontal-tumble

#### Spin up, drop down (explicit gravity)

Reels built `.direction('reverse')` roll upward, but `tumble({ gravity: 'forward' })` makes the tumble settle downward anyway. `gravity` is only worth setting when you want travel and settling to disagree; leave it at `'auto'` and a reverse reel drains upward with no further config.

That includes the cell stagger. `cellOrder` defaults to `'auto'`, which starts at the gravity-exit end. the edge symbols are leaving by. Under the explicit forward gravity here the bottom cell still goes first; drop the override and the top cell leads instead, because that is the edge the column now drains through. Pass `'endFirst'` or `'startFirst'` to pin a geometric end regardless of gravity.

Live demo (cascade-reverse-gravity): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#cascade-reverse-gravity

#### Drain upward (gravity follows travel)

The default case, for comparison: `.direction('reverse')` with no `gravity` key at all. Everything flips together. the top cell falls first and lands first, and the column peels upward behind it.

**Gotcha:** the server contract flips with it. Survivors pack against the edge gravity exits by, which is now the top, so `nextGrid` returns `[...survivors, ...fresh]`. Flipping the reel without flipping the grid is what makes an upward board look scrambled.

Live demo (cascade-drain-upward): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#cascade-drain-upward

#### Peek symbol from buffer-start

Pre-fill the `bufferStart` slot so a teaser symbol sits just out of frame, visible during the next spin's scroll-in.

Live demo (peek-from-above): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cascade/#peek-from-above

### Cells, bounds, paylines & overlays
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cells-and-banners/

Address individual cells, render your own paylines and overlays, and swap feature modes at runtime, each shown live below. For banner reels above the grid, see [orientation and direction](/recipes/orientation-and-direction/#horizontal-banner).

#### Cell bounds. overlays, paylines & hit areas

getCellBounds(reel, cell) hands you the pixel rect of any visible cell, for paylines, win outlines, or hit areas that align exactly with symbols.

Live demo (cell-bounds): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cells-and-banners/#cell-bounds

#### Cell hit areas. click to pick, hover to preview

Attach pointer events to individual cells with getCellBounds; hover previews, click toggles a pick, picks survive spins.

**Gotcha:** fill the hit rect with alpha 0, not `visible = false`. an invisible-but-filled rect is still hit-testable; a hidden one is not.

Live demo (cell-hit-areas): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cells-and-banners/#cell-hit-areas

#### Cell bounds on a horizontal set

`getCellBounds(reel, cell)` takes the same arguments on either axis, and (0, 0) is still the first cell of the first reel. The rect it returns transposes: on a horizontal set the reel index walks down the screen and the cell index walks across it, so the same cell index on every reel stacks vertically.

**Gotcha:** the payline drawn through those centres therefore runs vertically, where identical code draws a horizontal line on a vertical set. Read the rects; do not infer them from the indices.

Live demo (cells-horizontal-bounds): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cells-and-banners/#cells-horizontal-bounds

#### Hit areas on a horizontal set

The same `for reel, for cell` loop, with no orientation branch: the bounds are already screen-space, so the hit boxes land on the symbols either way. Hover previews, click toggles a pick, picks survive spins.

Live demo (cells-horizontal-hit-areas): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cells-and-banners/#cells-horizontal-hit-areas

#### Board primitive: build your own board

#### Draw paylines yourself from win:group

#### Paylines and payways with WinLines

`WinLines` from `pixi-reels/debug` draws a payline as one stroke through one cell per reel, and a payway as every winning cell joined to every winning cell on the next reel. Spins alternate between ten paylines, drawn as the presenter reaches each, and ways, every winning lattice at once.

Live demo (win-lines): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/cells-and-banners/#win-lines

### Feel: timings & landing FX
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/feel/
Tags: phases, steps, timing, fx, anticipation, speed, skip

The built-in phases run named step lists. `StartPhase` runs `delay, launch, pull, accelerate, announce`, `StopPhase` runs `delay, spinOut, land, bounce`, `AnticipationPhase` runs `tease`, and `f.register('stop', StopPhase, { steps })` hands you the list before it runs. These recipes are the feel work that used to mean a subclass: each is one `insertBefore` / `insertAfter` / `replaceStep`, or a list built by hand, and every one keeps slam and quicken working because the waits stay marked `cut`. The step API itself is on the [Phases page](/docs/api-phases/#steps).

#### Stagger curves

The flat stagger arrives as `ctx.config.delay` and the `delay` step is the only place it is spent, so a curve is one `replaceStep` per phase: the start ripples out from the middle reel, the stop's gaps grow so reels 1-3 fall fast and reel 5 hangs. The profile still owns the unit, and the second readout line is measured landings, not the schedule.

**Gotcha:** keep `{ cut: true }` on the replacement. It is a wait, and a quicken press must cut it the way it cuts the flat one.

Live demo (steps-stagger-curve): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/feel/#steps-stagger-curve

#### A wind-up launch

The built-in `pull` is a two-pixel twitch. Replace it with a real drag back, insert a `hold` after it, and the untouched `accelerate` ramps from wherever the reel is. Tap the readout to switch the wind-up off and compare.

**Gotcha:** cover both motion models the way the built-in does. Under the drive, name a `targetSpeed` and wait; under the tween, tween `reel.speed`. `reel.hasDrive` tells you which.

Live demo (steps-windup-start): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/feel/#steps-windup-start

#### A landing kick, with dust

One step after `land`, before `bounce`: the set kicks and a puff spreads under the reel, harder on the last one. The step returns nothing, so the bounce starts on the same frame. Return the tween and the phase waits for it: that is the difference between an effect and a beat.

**Gotcha:** a slam lands through `onSkip`, not through the list, so a step after `land` does not fire on a slam. FX that must play on a slam too hangs off `spin:reelLanded`. A quicken keeps the list.

Live demo (steps-land-impact): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/feel/#steps-land-impact

#### Beats and FX that follow the speed mode

`ctx.profile` is the profile the game registered under the active speed name, custom fields included. A `breath` beat before the spin-out and a `glow` after land both read the profile, so normal gets both and turbo gets neither, and the glow's fade rides `bounceDuration`. Tap the readout to switch speeds; the skip button here is `requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', speed: 'turbo' })`, which swaps the profile the same way.

**Gotcha:** a step never asks "is this turbo". Put the decision on the profile and every speed mode you add later comes with its own answer.

Live demo (steps-fx-per-profile): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/feel/#steps-fx-per-profile

#### A step you added, tuned from the profile

The recipe above puts a step's numbers on the profile as flat fields. They work and they are global: every phase sees them, and nothing says which phase they belong to. A **section** says it. Both steps here are inserted into `StopPhase`, and everything that shapes them lives under `stop`, keyed by the step's own name, with a `whenAnticipated` half the engine merges on top for a reel that teased — so reels 4 and 5 land on a deeper bounce and a heavier impact, and the same step draws them amber off `ctx.anticipated`. Nothing branches on the speed name.

```ts
stop: {
  steps: { breath: { duration: 140 }, impact: { lift: 8, duration: 420 } },
  whenAnticipated: { bounceDistance: 30, steps: { impact: { lift: 24 } } },
}
```

A step reads its own entry as `ctx.step`, in segment order: one object in the profile arrives as one entry, and a list is for a step written to consume segments. Declare the two names once, by merging into `StopSteps`, and `stop.steps` is checked and autocompleted like any built-in's.

**Gotcha:** `whenAnticipated` applies to a tease that ran to its END. Press skip mid-tease and that reel goes back to the section's own half — blue puff, small lift — because what the press cut is the tease the variant exists to pay off.

Live demo (steps-profile-sections): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/feel/#steps-profile-sections

#### A spotlight around the tease

`AnticipationPhase` runs one step and is created on the teased reel only, so "shade the other reels while the tease runs" is a list built by hand around the built-in: `[dim, ...steps, lift]`. Both wraps are awaited, 150 ms each, so the spotlight is on before the reel starts to crawl and off before the stop takes over.

**Gotcha:** a slam cancels the list in flight and `lift` never runs. Clear the shades on `spin:complete` as the backstop. A quicken cuts the `tease` step and `lift` still runs.

Live demo (steps-anticipation-spotlight): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/feel/#steps-anticipation-spotlight

#### One extra beat on the last reel

Every reel runs the same list, so a per-reel beat is a step that returns nothing on the reels it does not concern. `suspense` waits 700 ms before reel 5's spin-out and is instant on the others, pulsing the backlight while it waits.

**Gotcha:** a step that starts something must own it both ways out. `ctx.wait` resolves early when the step is cut, `ctx.signal` fires when it is cancelled; one `stop` handles the natural end, a quicken and a slam.

Live demo (steps-last-reel-suspense): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/feel/#steps-last-reel-suspense

#### Hold & Win: cells that spin sideways

The whole lock-and-respin round on `.axis('horizontal')`. Every cell is its own 1x1 ReelSet, so the axis only picks which edge a coin scrolls in from. the board still lays out cols x rows and the lock still claims one cell.

**Gotcha:** don't build this on a plain ReelSet with `.orientation('horizontal')`. there a reel IS a whole row, so the row travels as one ribbon straight across the cell gaps and past the cells that are supposed to be locked.

**Gotcha:** the ReelSet-level equivalent, `spin({ holdReels })`, holds a whole reel. a board has no `holdReels` because Hold & Win holds single cells.

#### Rectangular cells: width, height and a gap per axis

Hold & Win art is usually wider than tall. cellSize takes a width and a height plus a columnGap and a rowGap, so the board lays out to the art's own rectangle, with the game's grid showing through the gaps. Every clover here is a Spine 4.2 skeleton on the game's art, with idle, landing, win and blur tracks the engine drives through SpineReelSymbol.

Live demo (hold-and-win-rect-cells): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-rect-cells

#### Landing only, celebrate once

lockAnimation('landing') plays a settle on every lock and nothing else; board.playWin() is the one explicit celebration, fired when the game decides.

Live demo (hold-and-win-landing-only): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-landing-only

#### Clover base game into the feature

A fruit base game where gold clovers spin past showing bet-scaled money and the collect / multi / mystery / super clovers carry none; three or more clovers on the stop hand their cells to the Hold & Win board.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-base-game): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-base-game

#### Clover bonus board, 5x3

The feature on its own: gold clovers lock with their amounts, blanks are the game's dark clover tile, and the 1 2 3 lamps below are the respin counter.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-bonus): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-bonus

#### Draw order between cells

Every cell is its own reel set, so the clovers the engine lifts above the cells at rest share one layer, drawn in attach order: column by column, which lets the next column's clover cover a lower clover's glow. `cellZIndex` sorts that layer by whatever the board says - here lower rows in front and the capsule on top of everything, re-asked on every place and landing.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-cell-order): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-cell-order

#### One cell in front, for a beat

`cellZIndex` is the at-rest order and the board re-asks it on every place and every landing, so a clover that must not be overlapped while it upgrades cannot express that by returning a bigger number: the next landing overwrites it mid-animation. `board.lift(cell)` promotes the cell on a separate channel and hands back a release - the refresh keeps running underneath and cannot touch it, and the release restores the cell's place without recomputing anything.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-lift): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-lift

#### Lift one cell, dim the rest

`board.dim({ except })` is the partner of `lift()`: it draws above every cell's clover and below anything lifted, so a lifted cell stays in front of the dim whether or not it is excepted. A dim covers cells, not symbol ids - this collect resolves the gold clovers it is about to sweep to cells and spares them, so the money stays bright while the blanks go dark. It fades in and back out over `fade` ms off the board's own ticker, fast enough to belong to the beat rather than read as a transition; `fade: 0` cuts.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-lift-dim): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-lift-dim

#### Dim the cells, or dim only the art

Two channels for pushing a board back. `dim()` lays a rectangle over each cell, so the clover goes dark and so does the tile it sits in. `dimSymbols()` multiplies each symbol's own tint towards black instead: the art sinks and the board keeps its lights on. Same sweep runs twice below, so the only difference on screen is which one did it - `amount` is the strength on both, and both fade over `fade`.

The reason it is a board method rather than three lines of `gsap.to`: a dimmed cell that swaps its symbol has to keep its dim, and the symbol that left has to lose the tint before the pool hands it to another cell.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-dim-symbols): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-dim-symbols

#### Dimming the art is not dimming the cell

One slot blown up, with a fruit in it rather than a clover so the cell's own background shows all the way around the symbol. The blue plate is `cellChrome()` - the board draws it, it is not a symbol - so `dimSymbols()` never touches it however hard it dims the fruit. `amount` steps 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 and the plate does not move; then the same 0.6 through `dim()` takes the whole cell down.

The last beat is the corollary: swap the cell to the empty id and there is no art left to dim, so `dimSymbols()` changes nothing at all - not the symbol that has gone, and not the plate, which was never its business.

Which is the thing to watch for on a real board. If your blank tile is a registered symbol (as it is in the recipes above, where the dark tile is the `empty` id) then it IS art, and `dimSymbols()` dims it with everything else. Draw whatever must stay lit in `cellChrome()`, or name its cell in `except`.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-dim-one-cell): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-dim-one-cell

#### Clover bonus board, 5x5

The same board with five rows, every cell live from the start.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-bonus-5x5): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-bonus-5x5

#### Clover board that grows from 5x3 to 5x5

Built 5x5 with the top and bottom rows dormant behind the purple sealed tile (inactive); holding enough clovers opens a row with board.activate(), and the next respin spins it too.

The info argument also carries corners, that same per-cell object precomputed.

### Infinity reels: growing the board
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/infinity-reels/
Tags: expand, addReels, removeReels, addRows, multiways, ways, big-symbols, skip, win-lines

The base spin lands, then the board grows: `reelSet.expand({ columns })` adds the reels the server's result has beyond the base board, a step at a time, spinning only the new ones while everything before them holds. `addReels()` and `removeReels()` are the primitives under it; the next round shrinks back with `removeReels()`. The [infinity reels guide](/guides/infinity-reels/) is the short version: what the server sends, the calls, and the events.

#### One reel at a time

While the win still runs into the last reel, the server adds another reel to its result. Each step pans the camera to the new reel (`onStepAdded`), spins and lands it, then counts the ways and draws them with `WinLines` (`onStepLanded`).

**Skip:** the steps are one round. The first press slams the step in flight and turbos the rest, the same boost `skipSpin()` gives the rest of any round (a cascade-mode expansion lands its later steps at once instead, the way one press ends a cascade); the second aborts the expansion's `signal`, which lands every reel still to come in one step.

Live demo (infinity-reels): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels

#### Rows grow too

A wild on a new reel unlocks a row: `addRows(1, { cells })` in `onStepLanded` makes every reel one cell taller with the server's cells for the new row, and the reels after it arrive at the new height. The camera zooms out to fit, reading the board's size off `viewport.maskWidth` and `maskHeight`. The next round goes back with `removeReels()` and `removeRows()`.

**Gotcha:** rows change only between steps. Inside `onStepAdded` the step's reels are about to spin on columns sized for the board's old height, so `addRows()` throws there. A fast-forward (an aborted `signal`) lands every reel still to come in one step at the height the board has then, so this demo's skip slams a step at a time instead.

Live demo (infinity-reels-rows): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-rows

#### Stacked symbols that split

Q lands one cell tall or stacked two to four cells. When Q wins on every reel, each stack splits into more single Qs than it had cells, and its reel grows past the frame both ways. `reelSet.splitSymbol(reel, cell, ids)` places the server's split: the stack covering `(reel, cell)` becomes `ids`, one per cell, the cells above and below keep their symbols, and the board re-centres around the taller reel. While the win reaches the last reel, `expand()` adds another and the multiplier goes up by one. The next round goes back with `removeReels()` and `resetColumns()`. A reel that keeps its height instead, splits on MultiWays and a tap-to-split playground are on [Splitting symbols](/recipes/split-symbols/).

**Gotcha:** a split changes one reel's height, so the board re-centres around it. Hold the other reels still on screen (this demo moves its camera by their shift) and let the camera ease out, or they jump.

Live demo (infinity-reels-split): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-split

#### MultiWays: millions of ways

Each column's `visible.length` is that reel's shape, applied with `setShape()` for its step, so every reel the expansion adds multiplies the ways: eight reels of seven cells is 5,764,801 ways, ten is 282,475,249. Steps add two reels (`step: 2`).

Live demo (infinity-reels-multiways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-multiways

#### A big symbol widens its step

The steps add one reel each, but a 2x2 wild arrives in one of the columns. A one-reel step cannot land half a block, so that step adds two reels and the block lands whole. The plan is read from `symbolData` sizes and every block is validated before the first reel is added.

**Gotcha:** a block has to end on a reel the expansion adds. One that would run past the last of them, or past the bottom of a strip, throws before a reel is added.

Live demo (infinity-reels-big-symbol): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-big-symbol

#### Skip, reel groups and a protected tease

Press as often as you like and read the log. The base board is grouped (dashed boxes), so a press lands one group; each step's reel teases "will the win continue?" with `anticipation: { protect: 'once' }`, so the first press during a tease is spent and the next lands the reel; a press while the camera pans queues for the next step. The button calls `skipSpin()` and nothing else.

Live demo (infinity-reels-skip): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-skip

##### Picking a skip policy

- **Turbo the rest** (the default). The first `skipSpin()` frees the step in flight and boosts every later step to the fastest profile; the next round starts at normal speed again.
- **Slam each step.** Every press frees the step in flight. Presses during `onStepAdded` / `onStepLanded` (a camera pan, a win readout) are not lost: they free the next step as soon as it has its result.
- **Fast-forward.** Abort the expansion's `signal` and every reel still to come lands in one step. A quick-spin or autoplay mode can pass an aborted signal from the start: the whole expansion lands at once, with the same events and hooks.
- **Quicken instead of slam.** With `.skipMode('quicken')` (or `requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', speed: 'turbo' })`) a press shortens the step's spin but keeps its spin-out and bounce, so a long chain never looks cut.
- **Wide steps, one reel per press.** A step's reels arrive as one group. Call `setReelGroups()` in `onStepAdded` to split them, and each press frees one; or `slamStop({ reels: [...] })` lands part of a step and lets the rest play.
- **Keep the deciding tease.** `anticipation: (step) => stillWinning ? { protect: 'once', duration: 900 } : false` keeps the "will it continue?" tease through the first press, only on the steps where it matters.

**Gotcha:** `slamStop()` between steps has nothing to land, and a press after the last step has no step left: both are no-ops. A named `setDropOrder('ltr' | 'rtl' | 'all')` follows the reels that spin, so it covers the added reels and orders a step by place; a sticky `setStopDelays()` array covers only the reels it was given, and reels past its end stop with no delay.

#### What carries across steps

- **Events.** Each step fires the usual `spin:*` events for its own reels, plus `reels:added`, `expand:stepAdded` and `expand:stepLanded`, and `rows:added` when a hook grows the rows; the chain opens with `expand:start` and closes with `expand:complete` and then `expand:end` (`'complete'`, or `'failed'` when it threw). `reelSet.isExpanding` is `true` in between, so a `spin:start` listener can tell a step from a new round.
- **Stagger.** Start and stop delays count a reel's place in its step, not its index, so reel 40 does not wait forty delays.
- **Pins.** A sticky pin's turns and an `'eval'` pin belong to the round, so they are not spent per step.
- **Memory.** Reels are real reels while they are on the board; `removeReels()` destroys them and shrinks the viewport, mask and symbol pool back.

### Masks & board shapes
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/masks/
Tags: mask, rounded, silhouette, pyramid, jagged, frame

The viewport clips the reels through a `MaskStrategy` so buffer cells never leak past the grid. Everything here is additive; the default `RectMaskStrategy` is unchanged.

| Board | Strategy |
|---|---|
| Square frame art | `RectMaskStrategy` (default) |
| Rounded frame, reels flush | `RoundedRectMaskStrategy` (`scope: 'set'`) |
| Reels as separate cards, with a cross gap | `RoundedRectMaskStrategy` (`scope: 'reel'`) |
| Rounded frame, one rect per reel, any gap | `RoundedRectMaskStrategy` (`scope: 'outer'`) |
| Hold & Win board, a mask per cell | `cellMask((cell, { corners }) => ...)` |
| Pyramid / MultiWays, rounded, reels flush | `SilhouetteMaskStrategy` |
| Hexes, holes, cut-outs | `PathMaskStrategy` |

`inset(strategy, px)` and `composeMasks(a, b, ...)` wrap any of them, yours included.

#### A rounded window

`scope: 'set'` rounds the union bounding box. Safe at any cross gap, so it is the default.

Live demo (mask-rounded-set): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/masks/

#### Each reel as its own card

`scope: 'reel'` rounds every reel box instead.

**Gotcha:** needs a non-zero CROSS gap. At gap `0` neighbours share an edge and rounding both sides of it notches every seam. The strategy warns once.

Live demo (mask-rounded-reels): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/masks/#mask-rounded-reels

#### One rect per reel, the window's corners only

`scope: 'outer'` keeps one rect per reel, so buffer cells past a short reel stay hidden as with the default, and rounds a corner only where it sits on a corner of the union box: the first reel's outer pair, the last reel's outer pair, nothing in between. Inner edges stay square, so it is fine at cross gap `0`, where `scope: 'reel'` notches. `corners: { topLeft: true, ... }` narrows any scope to named screen corners.

**Gotcha:** on a jagged set the box corners may touch no reel, and then nothing rounds. Use `SilhouetteMaskStrategy` there.

Live demo (mask-outer-corners): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/masks/#mask-outer-corners

#### A mask per Hold & Win cell, from its row and column

Every Hold & Win cell is its own 1x1 reel set with its own mask, and `cellMask` takes a function called once per cell with `{ reel, cell }` (column, row) and `{ cols, rows, corners }`. Return any strategy per cell: here a plain rect everywhere and one rounded corner on each of the four corner cells, so a gapless board clips as one rounded window built from fifteen masks. `corners` is that per-cell corner set precomputed, for the short form `(_, { corners }) => new RoundedRectMaskStrategy({ radius, corners })`.

Live demo (hold-and-win-outer-corners): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/masks/#mask-hold-and-win-cells

#### Rounding a jagged board

A pyramid has no single rectangle to round: per-reel rounding notches the seams, bounding-box rounding hides the staircase. `SilhouetteMaskStrategy` walks the union outline and rounds every vertex, concave steps included via `concaveRadius`. A uniform set degrades to a rounded rect.

**Gotcha:** reels must butt together (cross gap `0`). With a gap they are genuinely disjoint; the strategy says so and falls back to per-reel rounded rects.

Live demo (mask-silhouette-pyramid): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/masks/#mask-silhouette

#### Any shape, without a class

`PathMaskStrategy` takes a `(graphics, context) => void`. The context carries `rects`, `width`, `height`, `axis` and `bleed`. Do not call `g.clear()` - the strategy already did.

**Gotcha:** `cut()` subtracts from the last shape already **filled**, so fill first. Draw the hole before filling and you get an empty mask and an invisible board, with no error.

Live demo (mask-path-custom): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/masks/#mask-path

#### Insetting and composing

`inset(strategy, px)` shrinks any strategy's output (negative grows) - the fix for art bleeding a pixel past the frame. Pass `{ top, right, bottom, left }` instead of one number when the frame's lips differ: `inset(new RoundedRectMaskStrategy({ radius: 43 }), { top: 4, bottom: 12 })`. Sides are screen sides in every orientation and an omitted side is untouched. `composeMasks(...)` unions several into the viewport's one mask, for a board plus a banner.

**Gotcha:** union only. A Graphics mask is the union of its filled shapes; there is no way to intersect or subtract two strategies. Use `.cut()` inside a `PathMaskStrategy` instead.

Live demo (mask-inset-compose): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/masks/#mask-inset-compose

#### A different trim per side

Frame art rarely has four equal lips. `inset(strategy, { top, right, bottom, left })` names the sides the way the artist measured them - screen sides in every orientation, an omitted side untouched - so a rounded window with a thick bottom lip is one wrapped strategy, not a hand-drawn path.

Live demo (mask-inset-sides): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/masks/#mask-inset-sides

#### Writing your own

Implement `build(ctx)` and `update(g, ctx)`, set `version = MASK_STRATEGY_VERSION`, pass it to `.maskStrategy(...)`. Reach for `PathMaskStrategy` first; a class only earns its keep when it holds state across draws.

Respect two things: `ctx.axis`, because `rects` are screen-space in every orientation (`axis.toLocal(w, h)` gives `{ cross, main }`), and `ctx.bleed`, which inflates the CROSS axis only. Add the optional `draw(g, ctx)` and your strategy composes like the built-ins.

`reelSet.skipNudge(reel)` fast-forwards a running nudge to its landed state; `nudge()` resolves normally, so the success path still runs.

Live demo (nudge-skip): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/nudge/#nudge-skip

### Orientation & direction
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/orientation-and-direction/
Tags: horizontal, orientation, direction, reverse, roll-up, banner, ways, axis

{/* The v1 standalone recipes redirect here; keep their fragments alive.
    `#horizontal-banner` needs no anchor - the heading below auto-slugs to it. */}

#### Horizontal banner

A one-reel sideways strip - the "paying symbols this round" banner. Just `.orientation('horizontal')` on the normal builder; same spin lifecycle, events, and speed profiles as a vertical set.

Live demo (horizontal-banner): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/orientation-and-direction/#static-spin-horizontal

#### Banner that joins a ways win

A horizontal banner above a 5x3 ways set. The banner is a sixth reel: a wild in the cell above a reel makes that reel count, extending the way. Two ReelSets in one container; the engine spins and lands both, the game scripts the ways math and spotlights the cells.

**Gotcha:** pixi-reels never computes wins - the recipe owns the ways evaluation and spotlight; the library only spins and lands.

Live demo (banner-ways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/orientation-and-direction/#banner-ways

#### Roll-up (reverse direction)

Every reel spins upward: one `.direction('reverse')` call. The same engine, events and landing bounce just run the other way.

Live demo (roll-up): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/orientation-and-direction/#roll-up

#### Mixed direction per reel

`.directionPerReel([...])` gives each reel its own travel direction for a woven, alternating look. Every reel still lands the exact server frame.

Live demo (roll-up-alternating): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/orientation-and-direction/#roll-up-alternating

#### Both knobs at once

Orientation is set-level and fixed at `build()`; direction is per reel. They compose, so a horizontal set can still alternate: here the strips run sideways and rows 0 and 2 scroll right while rows 1 and 3 scroll left.

**Gotcha:** a big symbol spanning more than one reel (`size.reels > 1`) cannot mix with mixed per-reel directions. The block coordinator assumes every reel a block covers feeds from the same edge, so `build()` throws rather than shipping a symbol that tears in half mid-spin. A uniform `directionPerReel` array is fine.

Live demo (orientation-horizontal-per-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/orientation-and-direction/#orientation-horizontal-per-reel

#### Read the axis instead of remembering it

Every reel exposes `reel.axis`: `orientation`, `direction`, `polarity`, `mainProp`, `crossProp`, and `feedEdge`. Projecting one step of travel back to screen space with `axis.toScreen(0, axis.polarity)` draws the arrows below with no orientation branch anywhere - the same three lines point down on a vertical forward reel and left on a horizontal reverse one.

**Gotcha:** `feedEdge` is derived from `polarity` and is never set twice. Read it (`'start'` forward, `'end'` reverse) when you need to know which side new symbols arrive from; do not track it yourself alongside `direction`.

Live demo (orientation-axis-readout): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/orientation-and-direction/#orientation-axis-readout

### Reel curvature
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/reel-curvature/
Tags: curve, curvature, perspective, projection, cylinder, drum, 3d

#### One number

A slot reel is a drum. The middle cell faces you; the outer ones have rotated away. A camera turns those into **trapezoids**, not smaller rectangles.

`.curve(amount)` - `0` flat (default, free), `1` hard barrel, most boards `0.3`&ndash;`0.5`. The grid on the tiles is the tell: lines converge on the outer rows, stay parallel on the middle one.

Live demo (curved-reels): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/reel-curvature/

```ts
builder.curve(0.45);                          // depth defaults to amount * 0.5
builder.curve({ amount: 0.45, depth: 0.35 }); // stronger perspective
```

`depth` is how much smaller an edge cell is than the middle. `0` is orthographic - cells bunch, nothing recedes or keystones. Capped just under `cos(arc)`, past which cells fold back over each other.

**The middle cell is never deformed.** Authored size, both axes, no keystone. So it cannot also fill a window sized for N flat cells: the ends fall short and the buffer cells show in that band. Frame it, like a cabinet bezel does - `curve.mapMain(0)` gives the depth.

#### Two ways to draw it

Every demo here uses `.curveMode('warp')`.

```ts
builder.curve(0.45).curveMode('warp').renderer(app.renderer);
```

| | `'symbol'` (default) | `'warp'` |
|---|---|---|
| Spine / composites bend | no | **yes** |
| Atlas art keystones | no | **yes** |
| Motion follows the curve | no | **yes** |
| Cost | free | 1 render pass per reel per frame |
| Sharpness | native | one resample |
| Needs `renderer()` | no | **yes** - `build()` throws |

`'warp'` renders each reel to a texture and displaces a mesh's **vertices**, so everything inside bends and no symbol cooperates. `'symbol'` projects each cell alone - crisper, but a `Container` transform is affine, so it only bends content that IS a texture.

The demo is Spine skeletons, which `'symbol'` cannot bend at all.

Live demo (curved-reels-warp): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/reel-curvature/#curved-reels-warp

Symbols that hang over their cell need two things: `SymbolData.zIndex` to stack within the reel, and `.curveBleed(px)` to stop the warp texture slicing the overhang at its edge.

```ts
builder.symbolData({ mystery: { zIndex: 2 } }).curveBleed(46);
```

#### Where the camera stands

One camera per reel, or one for the whole board. Outer reels tilt toward the middle; the centre one barely moves.

```ts
builder.curve(0.5).curveFocus('reel');     // default - five separate drums
builder.curve(0.5).curveFocus('set-lean'); // halfway, usually the sweet spot
builder.curve(0.5).curveFocus('set');      // one camera, one wide cylinder
```

Live demo (curved-reels-focus): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/reel-curvature/#curved-reels-focus

#### One drum, not five

`.curvePerReel([...])` gives each reel its own camera - bend the middle hardest, ease off outward. Length must equal `reels()`.

Live demo (curved-reels-per-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/reel-curvature/#curved-reels-per-reel

#### A pay band inside a taller drum

Five cells drawn, three paying. The outer rows exist to be curved - they are what makes it read as a cylinder rather than a grid. Better than a bare 3x5, where the drum must bend hard enough to distort the symbols people are reading; here the bend is spent on rows nobody reads, so it takes a deeper `curve(0.62)`.

Live demo (curved-reels-payband): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/reel-curvature/#curved-reels-payband

#### Cascades on a drum

The case the warp exists for: the bend is on the rendered reel, so explosions, survivors sliding down and drop-ins all ride the curve with the cascade code none the wiser.

A tumble board **must** frame the band. At the top it shows the buffer cell - the refill queue - which does not slide when survivors fall, so it sits frozen. At the bottom a pure tumble sets `bufferSymbols({ end: 0 })`, so there is nothing to show at all.

Live demo (curved-reels-cascade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/reel-curvature/#curved-reels-cascade

#### On real art

Playson's Supercharged Diamonds 3, the sheet the sprite Hold &amp; Win recipes use. Trimmed atlas frames: under `'symbol'` they could not keystone at all, under `'warp'` they bend like everything else. Blur-on-spin is unaffected.

Live demo (curved-reels-gems): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/reel-curvature/#curved-reels-gems

#### Numbers, not art

The pattern behind prize pickers and jackpot ladders. Symbols are drawn at runtime and the symbol id IS the amount, so `setResult([['100.00', ...]])` lands the value you name. Each cell is a `PIXI.Text` - a composite with no texture, so only the warp bends the digits.

Live demo (curved-value-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/reel-curvature/#curved-value-reel

#### Tuning it live

```ts
reelSet.setCurve(0.4);
reelSet.setCurve([0.2, 0.35, 0.5, 0.35, 0.2]);
reelSet.setCurve(0); // flat
```

#### Gotchas

- **Lifted symbols do not bend under `'warp'`.** `unmask: true`, the win spotlight, pin flights and overlays are outside the reel's texture, so they draw flat over a curved board. The builder logs when it sees `unmask`. `'symbol'` has no such split.
- **Leaning or bleeding cells cross their own column.** Anything but `curveFocus('reel')` auto-selects `SharedRectMaskStrategy`; with `curveBleed` under `'reel'`, set it yourself or the per-reel mask clips the overhang.
- **`getCellBounds()` returns the bounding box**, `getCellQuad()` the four corners drawn on. Outline with the quad, hit-test with the box.
- **The affine fallback owns `view.scale`.** A win animation tweening `symbol.view.scale` overwrites the projection while it runs - animate a child of `view`. Not an issue under `'warp'`.
- **Curvature is presentation only.** It never changes what lands where, `getVisibleGrid()`, or any event payload.

#### Extending `'symbol'` mode

Only if you skip the warp. The engine hands each symbol a projected quad via `ReelSymbol.applyCellQuad()`.

`SpriteSymbol` / `AnimatedSpriteSymbol` map it onto a `PerspectiveMesh` - true keystone, no extra render pass - when the texture owns its whole source. `canProjectTexture()` refuses atlas sub-frames: the mesh addresses its source with 0..1 UVs and remapping them onto the frame has not produced a correct draw here. Everything else gets a uniform scale sized to fit inside the quad, so no cell overlaps its neighbour and a `7` never becomes a squashed `7`.

Writing your own with a single texture? `PerspectiveCell` is exported and does the mesh plumbing. Art that does not fill its cell reports its real rect via `ReelSymbol.cellInset`, which the sprite symbols derive from the texture's trim.

### Skip & slam
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/
Tags: skip, slam, anticipation, tease, phases, timing, groups

A slam force-completes every phase, `AnticipationPhase` included - honest on an ordinary spin, and it hides the build-up on the spin that had one. These recipes are the levers that decide WHICH reels a press lands, and WHEN a reel may stop at all.

#### Land some reels, not all

`slamStop({ except: [3, 4] })` lands reels 0-2 now and leaves 3 and 4 to stop naturally.

**Gotcha:** a partial slam does not end the round - the button stays live, and only a full slam moves `skipStage` to `2` and applies the speed boost.

Live demo (skip-partial-slam): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-partial-slam

#### Name the reels that land

The complement: name the reels to land instead of the ones to spare. Here a three-beat plan walks the board outside in.

**Gotcha:** neither form needs guarding - out-of-range indices are ignored, and held or landed reels are never slammed.

Live demo (skip-reels-complement): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-reels-complement

#### A tease a press cannot hide

The same partial slam as a rule the engine applies for you. `protect: 'once'`: press 1 lands every non-tease reel and leaves the tease running, so the trigger symbols are on screen; press 2 ends it.

**Gotcha:** call `setAnticipation` BEFORE `setResult`. A press in the pre-result window is queued by `requestSkip()` and fires the moment the result arrives, so the tease must already be registered.

Live demo (protected-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-tease-protect

#### Walk the tease forward, one reel per press

The same rule per reel. Press 1 lands everything outside the tease; each press after releases the next tease reel. The player sets the pace.

**Gotcha:** release order is TEASE order, not reel index - `setAnticipation([4, 2, 3], ...)` releases 4 first.

Live demo (skip-stepwise-tease): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-stepwise-tease

#### Groups: reels that stop and skip together

Reel index is the engine's only ordering, and it cannot say "reels 1-2 land together, 3-4 tease one press each, reel 5 outlasts both". Reel 5 is index 4, so its stop delay comes due mid-tease.

```ts
reelSet.setReelGroups([[0, 1], [2, 3], [4]]);
reelSet.setAnticipation([2, 3], { stagger: 'sequential', protect: 'stepwise' });
// Presses walk the board: [1,2] -> 3 -> 4 -> [5].
```

A group is a barrier both ways. **Stopping:** no reel starts its stop sequence, anticipation included, until every reel in the earlier groups has landed - and it keeps spinning at full speed while it waits. **Skipping:** a press releases the next un-landed group, protection still applying inside it. Stop delays become group-relative; an explicit `setStopDelays()` still wins.

**Gotcha:** set it any time up to `setResult()` - the barrier is read as each reel's SpinPhase resolves - so a round can be grouped from its own server response. Every reel must appear exactly once, and changing the layout once reels have begun landing throws. `null` clears.

Live demo (reel-groups): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#reel-groups

For any other release order, use `protect: 'always'` and drive it yourself with `slamStop({ reels })` from a queue of your own.

**Gotcha:** two near-misses, both pinned by tests. Shrinking the set with `setAnticipation()` mid-spin does NOT release a teasing reel - the set is read once, as a reel leaves `SPIN`. And `setSpeed()` mid-spin does not re-time the round, which is why the `skipSpin()` boost lands on the NEXT spin.

#### A tease no press can end

Press 1 lands everything outside the tease, like `'once'`; every press after is a deliberate no-op. For when the tease IS the reward beat - a jackpot reveal, a final-reel bonus land.

**Gotcha:** a refused press emits no events rather than throwing, and `slamStop()` still lands everything. The engine refuses the player's press, never your own code's.

Live demo (skip-always-protect): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-always-protect

#### Your own release plan

`'always'` plus your own queue is the general form: the engine guarantees no press ends a tease behind your back, your code decides the groups. Three teasing reels, two beats.

Live demo (skip-custom-plan): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-custom-plan

#### A press that lands, not cuts

Every slam places the frame and lands in the same tick, so a press reads as a cut. `requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken' })` frees the same reels a slam would - protection, `'stepwise'` and groups all apply - and asks each for its landing instead: the tease ends, the stop delay is cut, the reel spins its frame in and bounces. `speed: 'turbo'` lands the quickened reels on the turbo spin-out and bounce; `builder.skipMode('quicken')` makes the mode the default.

**Gotcha:** a quicken is a skip. `skipStage` advances and `wasSkipped` is true, and `SpinResult.skipMode` says which mode ended the round. A `mode: 'slam'` press after it still cuts whatever is moving. Tap the readout to see the cut on the same spin.

Live demo (skip-quicken): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-quicken

#### Quicken with groups

The same barrier, a different mode. A quicken walks exactly the groups a slam would and quickens each one instead of placing it: a freed group goes violet (the stop, spinning in), not straight to grey. The cards are `PhaseCardSymbol`, so the phases are the colours.

**Gotcha:** a quickened reel counts as released for the WALK, so a fast next press is taken early; the reel behind the barrier still waits for the group before it to land. Reel 5 stays blue until reel 4 is down, however fast you press.

Live demo (quicken-groups): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#quicken-groups

#### Quicken first, slam second

One button, two presses: `requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', speed: 'turbo' })` on the first, `requestSkip({ mode: 'slam' })` on the second. A quicken press walks past the reels it already quickened; a slam press cuts them. Both are skips, and `SpinResult.skipMode` names the one that ended the round.

Each press carries a `payload` (`{ press: 1 }`, `{ press: 2 }`) and the HUD reads it back off `skip:requested`, with the profile a quicken named as `speed.name`: the event carries the whole press, the same context every phase's `onSkip(ctx)` gets, and `SpinResult.skipContext` keeps the last one.

**Gotcha:** read "has this round been quickened" off `skip:requested` and its `mode`, not off a local counter - a press that freed nothing must not arm the slam.

Live demo (quicken-then-slam): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#quicken-then-slam

#### A phase that can be quickened

`onSkip(ctx)` is where a custom phase hears a press, and `ctx.mode` is where it decides what to cut. This instant stop holds its frame a tenth of a cell short for 900 ms before sliding in; under `'quicken'` the hook kills the hold and slides at once, under `'slam'` it rests on the frame. The class declares `quickenable = true` to say its hook branches on the mode; without the flag a quicken leaves the phase alone and the reel still lands, the press just shortens nothing.

**Gotcha:** the quicken branch cuts a wait, never the landing itself - keep `land()` and `bounce()` exactly where the natural path has them, or a quickened reel lands differently from a patient one.

Live demo (quicken-custom-phase): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#quicken-custom-phase

#### Pressing before the server answers

`skipSpin()` throws before `setResult()` - there is nothing to land on. `requestSkip()` queues the intent and fires it when the result lands, protection intact. The demo's result is deliberately slow.

**Gotcha:** this is why `setAnticipation` comes BEFORE `setResult` - a queued press can only protect a tease the engine already knows about.

Live demo (skip-queued-request): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-queued-request

#### Driving the button from skipStage

`0` no press yet, `1` a press landed around a protected tease and left it running, `2` the round-ending press. Stage `1` needs protection, so an unprotected game still sees a two-state button. Read off `reelSet.skipStage` every frame, not counted locally.

Live demo (skip-stage-button): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-stage-button

#### No hold, no tease, nothing to protect

Turbo profiles set `anticipationDelay: 0`, and at a `0` ms hold `protect` does nothing - protecting a tease that never plays would stall the reels and put the response-time tell back. Spins alternate on one turbo profile; only `duration` differs.

Live demo (skip-turbo-inert): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-turbo-inert

#### Skip without a tell

Why you protect the tease rather than slow the skip down. Spins alternate scatterless and teasing, both auto-press at the same moment; the panel times the last non-tease reel. The numbers stay equal - what differs happens after the press, on screen.

Raising `minimumSpinTime` instead gets the pacing right and leaks the outcome through response time: the player learns a feature is coming from how the button felt.

Live demo (skip-no-tell): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-no-tell

#### Per-reel spin floor

No slam here. `minimumSpinTime` is one value on the speed profile, shared by every reel; `setMinimumSpinTime([0, 0, 0, 1000, 1000])` overrides it per reel, so reels 0-2 take the result on arrival while 3 and 4 hold a full second.

**Gotcha:** sticky across `spin()` and `refill()` until cleared with `null`, like `setStopDelays()`. Set it at boot, not per spin.

**Gotcha:** a floor governs NATURAL landings only. A slam ignores it, so a mid-spin tap lands all five together and the labels read `-> slam`.

Live demo (skip-min-spin-time): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-min-spin-time

#### Uniform floor, and clearing it

A single number raises the floor on every reel; `null` hands it back to the speed profile, which is not the same as a floor of `0`. Spins alternate so the difference reads back to back.

Live demo (skip-min-spin-uniform): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-min-spin-uniform

#### Cascades

Anticipation runs before the tumble/standard split, so a cascade spin teases and protects like a strip spin. Three things differ, all about what a press carries:

| | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Initial spin | `protect` applies unchanged. Press 1 lands the reels outside the tease, press 2 ends it. |
| Round side effect | In cascade mode this is auto-slam-refills, not a speed boost. A protected press does NOT spend it; the press that ends the tease does, and every refill after that lands instantly. |
| Refills | Carry no tease. `refill()` clears the anticipation set on entry, so a press inside one is an ordinary full slam - though `slamStop({ reels })` still works per reel there. |

**Gotcha:** a partial slam does not abort the chain, but it does mark the whole result `wasSkipped: true`.

Live demo (skip-cascade-protect): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#skip-cascade-protect

#### Hold & Win

Nothing to demo, and that is the point: a Hold & Win board is one single-reel `ReelSet` **per cell**, so `slamStop({ reels })` can only ever name reel `0`. The granularity you want is per cell - `BoardGrid.skipSpinning()` / `HoldAndWinBoard.skip()`.

Protection on a cell's set is consistent but rarely useful, since "every reel outside the tease" is empty:

- `'once'` - press 1 spends the protection and lands nothing, press 2 lands the cell. Working as intended.
- `'stepwise'` - the release group IS the tease reel, so one press lands it.
- `'always'` - **do not use it here.** No press can ever land the cell, and `BoardGrid.skipSpinning()`'s recovery path needs it to land or the next `respin()` throws.

#### Subclass a built-in phase

Every built-in phase is exported, so a small change is a subclass. `StopPhase` gains a landing backlight; sequencer, bounce and skip pose are inherited. Register under the same key to replace the built-in.

**Gotcha:** call `super` from every hook you override - a reel whose `onEnter` never reaches it spins forever. Override `onSkip` too if the beat should fire on a slammed reel.

Live demo (phase-subclass-stop): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#phase-subclass-stop

#### A spin floor the phase decides for itself

Subclass `SpinPhase` and a per-reel floor is one line. `setMinimumSpinTime([...])` is the ready-made version; subclass when the floor is derived rather than configured.

**Gotcha:** merge the config, don't replace it - `super.onEnter({ ...config, minimumSpinTime })`.

**Gotcha:** the staircase is natural landings only. A slam ignores the floor, so a mid-spin tap flattens it and the labels read `-> slam`.

Live demo (phase-subclass-spin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#phase-subclass-spin

#### Using update() from a subclass

A per-reel countdown drawn from inside the tease: `onEnter` shows the label then calls `super`, `update(deltaMs)` runs every frame, `onSkip` clears it when a press force-completes the phase.

**Gotcha:** `update` accumulates ticker time, not wall clock, so it stays correct in a backgrounded tab. The active `SpeedProfile` is already on `this._speed`.

Live demo (phase-subclass-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#phase-subclass-anticipation

#### A phase written from scratch

Extend `ReelPhase` for the whole behaviour rather than a tweak - here a flat linear ramp with no step-back pull, replacing `StartPhase`.

**Gotcha:** a custom name buys nothing. The controller only asks for lifecycle keys, so `register('myPhase', ...)` is orphaned - take the key instead. And call `this._complete()` exactly once, or the spin promise never settles.

Live demo (phase-from-scratch-start): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#phase-from-scratch-start

#### Phases that take constructor arguments

The cascade phases and `AdjustPhase` take build-time config as extra constructor arguments, so a subclass needs `registerFactory` and must forward them. `resolveTumbleConfig(config)` builds the shape they expect.

**Gotcha:** `.phases(...)` sits before `.tumble(...)` here and still wins - configurators are deferred to `build()` and applied after the built-in registrations.

Live demo (phase-subclass-cascade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/skip/#phase-subclass-cascade

See [Phases](/docs/api-phases/) for the full extension contract.

### Splitting symbols
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/split-symbols/
Tags: split, splitSymbol, setColumn, resetColumns, ways, multiways, stacked-symbols

When a symbol splits, the cell it stands on becomes two or more cells of their own. `reelSet.splitSymbol(reel, cell, ids, { height })` places the server's split: the symbol covering `(reel, cell)` becomes `ids`, one per cell, and the cells above and below keep their symbols. Any symbol one reel wide splits, in any slot: a 1x1, or a stacked big symbol in full view. It returns `{ reelIndex, from, count }`, the new cells, so the game can animate them. `height` says what gives:

- `'grow'` (the default): the cells keep their size and the reel grows. The board re-anchors around it per the builder's `reelAnchor`.
- `'keep'`: the reel keeps its height and every cell on it shrinks to share it, as a MultiWays reel's do. Nothing else moves. It is the default on MultiWays, where a reel's height is fixed.

`resetColumns()` puts every reel back to the cells it was built with, at their size. `setColumn(reel, column, { height })` is the primitive under both: one reel shows a column of any length. The [infinity reels guide](/guides/infinity-reels/#stacked-symbols-that-split) has the short version.

#### Grow or keep

Both boards land the same result and split the same cells, one copy at a time. On the left the reel grows; on the right it keeps its height and its cells shrink. The titles read each reel's cells and height off the engine.

**Gotcha:** under `'keep'` every symbol on the reel is resized, so its art has to draw at any cell height, as MultiWays art already does. These boards anchor their reels at the top (`reelAnchor('start')`), so a reel grows downward; with the default `'center'` it grows both ways and the board re-centres.

Live demo (split-modes): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/split-symbols/#split-modes

#### Tap a cell to split it

Tap any cell and it splits in two; the readout prints the exact call. Pick `grow` or `keep` above the board. Spin to start over: `resetColumns()` runs first.

Live demo (split-tap): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/split-symbols/#split-tap

#### Split in place on MultiWays

On MultiWays a reel's height is fixed, so a split makes room inside it, and the ways go up with the count. The server names the winning symbol and which of its cells split, into two or three copies each, and `WinLines` draws the ways after every split.

**Gotcha:** the count stays within the set's `[minCells, maxCells]`, as a `setShape()` would. Raise `multiways({ maxCells })` to split further. The next spin's `setShape()` reshapes every reel from wherever its split left it.

Live demo (split-in-place): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/split-symbols/#split-in-place

#### Stacked symbols on infinity reels

A stack two to four cells tall splits into more single symbols than it had cells, its reel growing past the frame both ways while `expand()` adds reels. That demo is on the [infinity reels page](/recipes/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-split).

**Gotcha:** a reel a block wider than one reel covers cannot change on its own, or the block's reels stop lining up, so `splitSymbol()` and `setColumn()` throw there. Every demo here splits a symbol one reel wide.

### Starters
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/starters/
Tags: starter, 5x3, cascade, multiways, hold-and-win, horizontal, reverse, orientation

Canonical starting templates. copy one, swap in your art and math, and ship.

#### Classic 5×3 starter

The copy-paste starting point for a left-to-right line-pay slot, the foundation of most slot games.

Live demo (classic-5x3): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/starters/#classic-5x3

#### Cascade 6x4 tumble

Modern tumble/cascade slot on runCascade; card symbols first, then the identical build with real Spine art.

Live demo (cascade-6x5): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/starters/#cascade-6x5
Live demo (cascade-6x5-spine): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/starters/#cascade-6x5

#### MultiWays

Per-spin cell variation: each reel lands on a different cell count between minCells and maxCells, and total ways is the product of the per-reel cell counts.

**Gotcha:** call reelSet.setShape(rowsPerReel) BEFORE setResult(), with serverGrid[i].length === rowsPerReel[i].

Live demo (multiways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/starters/#cascade-6x5

#### Hold & Win respin

Coins lock on land and respin until the grid fills; board events drive the HUD.

Live demo (hold-and-win): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/starters/#hold-and-win

#### Horizontal starter

The same template with the strips turned sideways: three reels stacked down the screen, each scrolling along X. One call, `.orientation('horizontal')`, plus the cell size you want on screen.

**Gotcha:** `symbolSize(w, h)` and `symbolGap(x, y)` stay screen-space here, so on a horizontal set the strip advances by the symbol WIDTH and `x` is the gap between cells while `y` is the gap between reels. Index space does not move: `reels(3).visibleCells(5)` and the `ColumnTarget[]` you pass `setResult()` are unchanged.

Live demo (starter-horizontal-5x3): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/starters/#starter-horizontal-5x3

#### Reverse starter

Classic 5x3, travelling the other way: symbols rise and each reel lands from below. The whole diff against the classic starter is `.direction('reverse')`.

**Gotcha:** buffers stay geometric. `bufferStart` is still the slot above the window, so on a reverse reel the "next up" slot is `bufferEnd`. Read `reel.axis.feedEdge` rather than assuming. See [orientation and direction](/recipes/orientation-and-direction/#roll-up) for the per-reel and mixed-axis variants.

Live demo (starter-reverse-5x3): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/starters/#starter-reverse-5x3

### Symbols, layering & motion blur
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/symbols/
Tags: symbols, reveal, mystery, pools, buffers, weights, layering, static-spin, motion-blur, spine, horizontal, orientation

Symbol building blocks and how they are drawn: the classes you register, the three ways to layer overflowing art, and spinning on cached blur textures.

#### CardSymbol. debug / prototyping helper

No-asset PIXI.Graphics symbol for recipes, mechanic tests, and prototypes; crisp at any cell size.
Exported from the package, so a prototype needs no art at all:
`import { CardSymbol, CARD_DECK, WILD_CARD } from 'pixi-reels'`.

**Gotcha:** debug scaffolding, not production art - ship SpriteSymbol / AnimatedSpriteSymbol / SpineSymbol instead.

Live demo (card-symbol-debug): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/recipes/symbols/#card-symbol-debug

#### PhaseCardSymbol: read the phase off the board

A `CardSymbol` that is grey at rest and takes the colour of the phase its reel is running - sky for `start`, blue for `spin`, amber for `anticipation`, violet for `stop`, a green beat on landing. Register it like any symbol, then point one watcher at the reels: `PhaseCardSymbol.watch(reelSet.reels)` paints every card from the reels' own `phase:enter`, `landed` and `symbol:created` events, custom phases included, and returns the release.
